subject: Order Form billing visibility & commit reallocation
messages:
From: James Wong <james.wong@astercloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: AsterCloud Billing <finance@astercloud.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form v2 — billing split & commit reallocation

Marcus —

Thanks for the call yesterday. We reviewed the Order Form v2 and have two questions before we can route for PO approval:

1) Billing visibility: can you provide a clear invoice cadence if we split the $1M annual commit across regions? We need to understand invoice dates for each entity (US vs EMEA) so our accounting team can map cashflow.

2) Commit reallocation: we'd like the ability to reallocate up to 20% of the committed tokens between regions each quarter without triggering an amendment. Is that possible from an invoicing/ordering perspective or will that require a formal Order Form change each time?

Attached: AsterCloud_OrderForm_v2.pdf (redline comments inline).

Appreciate a quick write-up we can share with our finance lead.

—James
James Wong
Director, Cloud Ops
AsterCloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: James Wong <james.wong@astercloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form v2 — billing split & commit reallocation

James —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Short answers up front: we can provide per-entity invoice visibility and we can support a limited quarterly reallocation if we define a reallocation window and an internal notification process; that approach avoids an Order Form amendment for every move. Below is a proposed operational model you can share with finance:

Option A — Staggered invoicing (recommended):
- Invoices issued monthly by entity based on committed tokens allocated to that entity at the start of each quarter.
- Reallocation window: first 10 business days of each quarter; allocations submitted via a short form and copied to both billing teams.
- Up to 20% reallocation allowed per quarter without amendment; moves beyond that trigger an Order Form revision.

Option B — Centralized invoice + internal allocation:
- Redwood issues a single invoice to the master buying entity; AsterCloud provides internal allocation schedule for your internal accounting. (This is simpler contractually but requires your AP to accept a single invoice.)

Net terms: We can keep Net45 per the draft Order Form. Taxes: Redwood will invoice gross; tax responsibility will follow the invoiced entity unless you provide tax exemption documentation.

Next steps if you like Option A: Kimberly (cc'd) will formalize the billing cadence as an appendix to the Order Form (payment schedule matrix) and Ben will confirm the legal/legal ops redline path for the reallocation language so your procurement team can accept that flexibility.

I can also prepare a simple two-paragraph summary for your AP to attach to the PO.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: James Wong <james.wong@astercloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form v2 — billing split & commit reallocation

James —

Following Marcus's note, attached is a draft payment_schedule_matrix.xlsx that maps the staggered invoicing option (Option A) across the US and EMEA entities. Key items we suggest adding as an appendix to the Order Form:

- Quarterly allocation window and submission process (form + confirmation email).
- Cap on intra-quarter reallocations (20% without amendment).
- Invoice issuance timeline (invoices generated on day 5 of each month for the prior month; any allocation changes submitted in window will be reflected starting the following month).
- PO numbering expectations and preferred remit-to for each entity.

A couple of asks for your AP team to confirm:
1) Which legal entity will hold the PO and accept the invoices? (If you want us to route invoices to multiple entities we need entity legal names and remit addresses).
2) Any tax-exemptions or VAT registration numbers we should apply per region.

Ben — can you confirm whether the reallocation allowance as drafted will be treated as an operational appendix (billing schedule) or if Legal prefers we bake precise reallocation language into the Order Form main body? I'd like to keep this flexible but auditable.

Kimberly Park
Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: payment_schedule_matrix.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: James Wong <james.wong@astercloud.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 19:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form v2 — billing split & commit reallocation

Team / James —

Thanks — this approach looks workable. From a contracts perspective I recommend we: 

1) Add a short "Billing Allocation Appendix" to the Order Form that references the payment schedule matrix and the quarterly reallocation window. That gives finance the operational flexibility and keeps the main MSA/Order Form clean.
2) Include a single sentence in the Order Form stating reallocations <=20% per quarter are permitted when submitted within the defined window; anything outside requires an amendment.
3) Ask AsterCloud to provide the remit-to and the exact legal entity names now so we can mirror them in the appendix and produce an invoice example for your AP.

James — once we get the remit/legal names and any VAT/GST numbers, I'll run a final redline and circulate a doc for signature. If you're ready, we can send a DocuSign packet with the Order Form + appendix.

Ben Carter
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
